C-AICC-DEPLOY.IntentSummary: Build the standard-library-only Rust tool deploy/aicc-deploy that mirrors html/aicc into the deploy repository, writes a hashed manifest, and with an explicit flag commits, pushes origin then websvc, and verifies the served manifest, defaulting to a dry run and refusing unsafe states.

T-001.Title: Create the crate with SHA-256, manifest, and tree-diff logic

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: deploy/Cargo.toml defines the aicc-deploy binary with no dependencies, and .gitignore ignores deploy/target.
The SHA-256 implementation matches the standard test vectors for empty input, abc, and a multi-block input.
A tree scanner lists files under a directory with relative paths and hashes in sorted order, and a diff function reports added, changed, and removed files.
The manifest writer produces stable JSON listing each file with its SHA-256 and size plus the source commit, and identical input gives identical bytes.
The tool runs portal/tools/check.py --idempotent in the source repository and stops if it fails, so a stale or broken html/aicc is never published.

It stops when tracked files in the source repository are modified, when the deploy path is not a git repository, when the deploy branch is not main, when the origin or websvc remote is missing, or when the deploy repository has changes outside html/aicc.
Each refusal prints one clear message and exits non-zero before any write.

T-003.Title: Implement mirroring and the commit-and-push flow

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Applying a sync copies added and changed files, deletes removed files and empty directories under the deploy repository's html/aicc, writes package-manifest.json there, and touches nothing else.
Publishing stages only html/aicc, commits with a message naming the source commit, and pushes origin and then websvc, stopping if the first push fails.
When there are no differences, no commit is made and nothing is pushed.
The tool never force-pushes and never changes git configuration.
A plain HTTP GET client built on the standard library fetches package-manifest.json from the served URL, follows no redirects, and handles a chunked or content-length response.
Verification retries for a bounded time and succeeds only when the served manifest equals the published manifest. Otherwise it reports the difference and returns failure.
A unit test runs the client against a local test server.

T-005.Title: Add the command line and the integration test

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The command line has --dry-run as the default, --publish, --no-origin, --source, --deploy-repo, --url, --branch, --skip-verify, and --help, with defaults for this host recorded in one place.

An integration test creates a temporary source tree and deploy repository with a local bare repository as both remotes, then checks the first publish, a stale file removal, a no-change second run, and each refusal case, and confirms no file outside html/aicc changed.
The dry run prints added, changed, and removed files and a summary, and exits zero without writing.

T-006.Title: Document the tool and run it in dry-run mode against the real repositories

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: deploy/README.md explains what the tool does, its flags, the publish sequence, how the push to websvc triggers the server hook, and how to roll back with git revert.
A dry run against /devops/obank/aicc/html/aicc and /devops/websvc/websvc-ob-aicc leaves both repositories unchanged, verified by comparing git status and a tree hash before and after.
The dry-run output is saved under deploy/verification/.
